findings.title: Pre/post source equality does not establish the actual input of the review/test
findings.evidence: The selected procedure checks materialized HEAD and tracked-source manifest before and after execution, rejecting dirty tracked sources. Both samples can match the artifact when a build task, supported hook or generator changes a tracked source, the verifier consumes the changed bytes, and the task restores the original bytes before the final sample. Separate repositories prevent executor/sibling dependence but do not prevent this unit-local mutate-and-restore case. Native read-only capability is only used where supported, and there is explicitly no enforcing outer sandbox.
findings.requirement: Approved R2 lines 63-70 requires actual materialized SHA/source versions and states that the reviewer's/verifier's own test/build writes must not select a different reviewed revision. This is an own-unit write case, rather than the explicitly excluded arbitrary external same-user mutation case.
findings.impact: The design currently permits evidence to be associated with an artifact SHA even though the actual reviewed/tested tracked input differed during execution.
findings.requested_change: Specify the supported unit-local source-write/input policy and its real prevention, detection or before-effects refusal mechanism. If a supported tool requires changed tracked input, distinguish that input/result from exact-artifact verification. Add a mutate-consume-restore control in addition to persistent-dirty checks. No universal same-user filesystem sandbox or arbitrary external-writer attribution is requested.
findings.verification: Static reasoning from the selected procedure; no native/test execution or reproduced production failure claimed.

findings.title: The migration does not specify a fence for already-open schema 3 Store writers
findings.evidence: Baseline Store::initialize checks user_version only when opening the connection (crates/rrx/src/state/mod.rs:79-85). Its generic write_snapshot performs versioned UPDATE of retained tables without rechecking schema or owner epoch (lines 1629-1655), and append_event similarly writes without an epoch check (1657 onward). The proposed v4 retains those tables. An old connection opened before migration can therefore continue a legacy write after user_version is advanced. The new state-root file lock/owner IPC is not implemented by that old binary, so it does not itself fence the old connection.
findings.requirement: Approved R8 lines 203-210 requires authoritative transition fencing and that old readers reject the newer schema rather than silently write it.
findings.impact: A normal overlapping legacy client/runtime can write old-format authority into retained tables after the new runtime begins schema 4 scheduling. Reopen refusal alone does not satisfy the selected single-owner/migration contract.
findings.requested_change: Define how migration fences incompatible already-open legacy readers/writers, or define the concrete quiescence/drain prerequisite and refusal path before committing the upgrade. Cover an old Store connection opened before migration and a post-upgrade legacy write, not only old-binary reopen. This does not require proving native process death or resisting raw same-user database tampering.
findings.verification: Baseline Git source and design inspected read-only; no migration or production test run.

prior_dispositions.evidence: Section 5 lines 223-252 explicitly says pre/post hashes are diagnostics, not transient-mutation proof. SnapshotManager makes tracked source directories/files and pinned Git input read-only before dispatch, with separate output paths and no writable fallback. Native reviewers require the supported read-only capability; verifiers require qualified output profiles. Mixed source/output, aliases and incompatible hooks refuse the profile; derived-output profiles must record/validate actual inputs/tools/digests. The ordinary mutate-consume-restore control must fail at its first source write. chmod/raw bypass is explicitly uncovered and cannot qualify R2. This addresses ordinary supported own-tool mutation without asserting universal same-user enforcement. Actual permission/profile and mutate-consume-restore controls are Phase2/3 gates, not observed passes.

Section 3 lines 124-140 separately handles pre-open schema 3 writers: BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE guards cover every existing/new mutable application table and call the per-connection zero-argument version function. New writers register the safe innocuous trigger-usable function; old connections lack it. The selected tests cover cached/fresh writes, REPLACE, old read-to-write snapshots, missing-function refusal and positive new-writer behavior. Guard registration/coverage failure refuses migration. The design does not mistake DB fencing for terminating old native effects. SQLite primary contracts support connection-local registration, schema-change recompilation and write/snapshot isolation; actual bundled rusqlite behavior remains explicitly unverified until Phase2.

regression_assessment.natural_terminal_and_cleanup: Section 2 lines 63-70, state-machine terminal row, capture publication protocol and section 9 lines 424-430 distinguish native_effects_open from result_finalization_open. Reliable natural terminal closes native input/tool/grant authority while retaining Runtime-only capture authority. Cancellation/replacement/epoch fencing close both. Publish closes finalization; capture failure requires durable draft/unresolved disposition. Janitor process observations may run, but destructive input/worktree/branch disposal and dependent path release await finalization closure and retention. The new concurrent-janitor control explicitly checks this race. No new native turn, remote grant or known-work-to-Lost inference is permitted by finalization.
regression_assessment.semantic_authority: Fresh Task write CAS during status/wait updates remains combined with unit/generation/phase authority; source freshness, P/G activity/version, Workflow reservations and permission policy remain required. This design clarification is not a general stale-unit bypass.
regression_assessment.best_effort_boundary: Cookie-discovered numeric PID signalling remains disabled when atomic identity cannot be maintained. Selected safe owned-child/group cleanup is not all-descendant death. Unknown resources/remote effects retain scoped reconciliation. Same-user permission/raw path bypass and host/storage failure remain explicit limits.
